subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow stale OpenAI route/doctor-owner repair first, folded into the broader shared session-state resolver, or treated as expected behavior when the session was explicitly switched to OpenAI?
rationale: Source proves DeepSeek should not be claimed directly by Codex, but the live report mixes Codex hot reload, persisted selected model state, and an explicit `/model openai` clarification, so automation should not choose the permanent session-state contract alone.

options.title: Fix narrow route drift first
options.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal OpenAI route cleanup while keeping the broader shared resolver as follow-up.

options.title: Fold into shared resolver
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87957 as the canonical owner and copy this DeepSeek/Codex hot-reload case into its acceptance criteria.

options.title: Treat explicit OpenAI selection as expected
options.body: Keep Codex-for-OpenAI behavior and improve status/doctor diagnostics if maintainers decide the report is only an explicit `/model openai` session.

recommendation.title: Fix narrow route drift first
recommendation.body: Repair stale auto OpenAI session pins and literal OpenAI route cleanup while keeping the broader shared resolver as follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, Codex routing, and selected session model resolution.
